column3: “the person with the scaly infection” renders “the one plagued with the scall.”
“a faint white” renders “a dull white,” and “eczema” renders “bohaq,” a harmless rash.
“at the front and sides” renders “from the side of his face.”
“shall surely pronounce him unclean” renders an emphatic doubled verb.
“the leper” renders “the one with tsara’at,” and “shall be uncovered” renders “shall be let loose.”
“leprosy” renders “tsara’at,” here a mold or mildew in fabric or leather (also in verses 49–59).
“quarantine the article with the mark” renders “shut up the mark.”
“a leprous malignancy” renders “a malignant tsara’at” (also in verse 52).
“changed its appearance” renders “turned its eye”; the last clause, “an eating away … on the top or on the front,” renders a difficult phrase whose meaning is uncertain.
